title: TESSERACT: Eliminating Experimental Bias in Malware Classification across Space and Time
authors: Feargus Pendlebury; Fabio Pierazzi; Roberto Jordaney; Johannes Kinder; Lorenzo Cavallaro
dataset: Android apps: ~129k samples (AndroZoo) spanning 2014-2016, labelled via VirusTotal (details Sec. 2.2); ~10% malware in realistic setting
method: Evaluation framework; constraints C1 (temporal training consistency), C2 (temporal goodware/malware window consistency), C3 (realistic malware-to-goodware ratio in testing); new metric AUT (area under time); tuning algorithm for training class ratio; re-evaluation of three published classifiers (linear SVM on Drebin features, Random Forest on MaMaDroid Markov features, a deep net)
eval_protocol: Time-aware splits with monthly test periods over 24 months; compares 10-fold CV (biased) vs temporally consistent evaluation; varies malware ratio in train/test

title: TESSERACT: Eliminating Experimental Bias in Malware Classification across Space and Time (Extended Version)
authors: Zeliang Kan; Shae McFadden; Daniel Arp; Feargus Pendlebury; Roberto Jordaney; Johannes Kinder; Fabio Pierazzi; Lorenzo Cavallaro
dataset: Android: 259,230 samples over five years (abstract); additional case studies on Windows PE and PDF malware
method: Extended TESSERACT: constraints, AUT metric, training-data tuning, plus delay-decay mitigation strategies (active learning, rejection, incremental retraining) compared across domains
eval_protocol: Time-aware evaluation with AUT over multi-year windows; cross-domain (Android, PE, PDF)

title: Transcend: Detecting Concept Drift in Malware Classification Models
authors: Roberto Jordaney; Kumar Sharad; Santanu K. Dash; Zhi Wang; Davide Papini; Ilia Nouretdinov; Lorenzo Cavallaro
dataset: Android (Drebin and Marvin datasets) and Windows malware families (Sec. 5)
method: Conformal-evaluator framework: non-conformity measures and p-value-based credibility/confidence to detect when a deployed classifier's decisions are no longer supported by training data; rejection of drifting samples
eval_protocol: Train on older data, test on newer; measures how rejection thresholds trade off kept-accuracy vs rejected fraction

title: Transcending TRANSCEND: Revisiting Malware Classification in the Presence of Concept Drift
authors: Federico Barbero; Feargus Pendlebury; Fabio Pierazzi; Lorenzo Cavallaro
venue: 2022 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (S&P)
dataset: Android malware over time (AndroZoo-derived, time-stamped) and other drift settings (Sec. VI)
method: TRANSCENDENT: formal treatment of conformal evaluation; two new conformal evaluators (inductive, cross-conformal) that are cheaper than the original transductive one; classification-with-rejection under drift
eval_protocol: Time-aware train/test with rejection; compares rejection quality against baselines (probability thresholds, etc.)

title: Continuous Learning for Android Malware Detection
authors: Yizheng Chen; Zhoujie Ding; David Wagner
dataset: Android apps over a 7-year period (AndroZoo-based, time-stamped)
method: Hierarchical contrastive learning plus a new active-learning sample-selection strategy to maintain a drifting classifier with limited analyst labels
eval_protocol: Train on one year, deploy over subsequent months/years with a monthly labelling budget; compares against prior active-learning baselines

title: Sunrise to Sunset: Analyzing the End-to-end Life Cycle and Effectiveness of Phishing Attacks at Scale
authors: Adam Oest; Penghui Zhang; Brad Wardman; Eric Nunes; Jakub Burgis; Ali Zand; Kurt Thomas; Adam Doupé; Gail-Joon Ahn
dataset: One year of victim traffic to phishing pages impersonating a major financial brand (PayPal), via the 'Golden Hour' passive monitoring framework; 4.8M victim visits
method: Large-scale measurement of the phishing life cycle: deployment, email lure, victim visits, detection by the ecosystem, account compromise
eval_protocol: Longitudinal measurement; timing analysis of campaign phases relative to blacklist detection

title: PhishTime: Continuous Longitudinal Measurement of the Effectiveness of Anti-phishing Blacklists
authors: Adam Oest; Yeganeh Safaei; Penghui Zhang; Brad Wardman; Kevin Tyers; Yan Shoshitaishvili; Adam Doupé; Gail-Joon Ahn
dataset: 2,862 researcher-deployed, innocuous PayPal-branded phishing sites across six deployments over nine months
method: Controlled, longitudinal experiments measuring blacklist speed, coverage and consistency; reproduces evasion techniques seen in the wild
eval_protocol: Time-to-blacklist measurement per browser/platform; evasion vs. non-evasion arms

title: On Designing and Evaluating Phishing Webpage Detection Techniques for the Real World
authors: Samuel Marchal; N. Asokan
venue: 11th USENIX Workshop on Cyber Security Experimentation and Test (CSET 18)
dataset: Position/guidelines paper; no new dataset
method: Guidelines for ground-truth composition, evaluation metrics and temporal-resilience testing of phishing webpage detectors
eval_protocol: Recommends: legitimate set must include unpopular/long-tail sites, URLs with paths (not just FQDNs from Alexa/DMOZ), real-world class distribution (about 1 phish per 100 benign) to avoid base-rate fallacy, test set larger than training set, and temporal-resilience tests (train at time t, test on later pages)

title: Evaluating and Combating the Impact of Concept Drift on the Performance of Machine Learning-Based Phishing Detection Systems
authors: Warren Fernando; Nikos Komninos
dataset: Public phishing/spam email corpora (the paper is email-centric, not URL-centric; see PDF Sec. 2-4)
method: Statistical framework (adapted from the FeSAD ransomware drift framework) to quantify similarity of phishing vs benign samples and flag drifted samples; feature-robustness analysis across time
eval_protocol: Temporal evaluation across dataset periods with drift scoring

title: Life-long phishing attack detection using continual learning
authors: Asif Ejaz; Adnan Noor Mian; Sanaullah Manzoor
dataset: Self-collected phishing and benign web pages for 2018, 2019, 2020, split into six temporally ordered datasets
method: Continual-learning (CL) algorithms on a vanilla neural network over FastText embeddings of HTML content, compared with static training and transfer learning
eval_protocol: Train on earlier period, test on later periods; measures deterioration over time

title: An Efficient Framework for Phishing URL Detection Using Adaptive Drift-Aware Feature Monitoring and Online Learning
authors: Sruthi Krishnan; Manohar Naik S
dataset: Real-time phishing URLs from PhishTank (abstract); benign source not stated in abstract
method: Kolmogorov-Smirnov drift detection on feature distributions plus online SGD updates
eval_protocol: Not specified in abstract beyond 'validation using real-time phishing URLs from PhishTank'

title: Dos and Don'ts of Machine Learning in Computer Security
authors: Daniel Arp; Erwin Quiring; Feargus Pendlebury; Alexander Warnecke; Fabio Pierazzi; Christian Wressnegger; Lorenzo Cavallaro; Konrad Rieck
dataset: Literature study of 30 top-tier security papers (2010-2020) plus four impact case studies (mobile malware, vulnerability discovery, source-code authorship, network intrusion detection)
method: Taxonomy of ten pitfalls: P1 sampling bias, P2 label inaccuracy, P3 data snooping, P4 spurious correlations, P5 biased parameter selection, P6 inappropriate baseline, P7 inappropriate performance measures, P8 base rate fallacy, P9 lab-only evaluation, P10 inappropriate threat model; prevalence survey and author feedback
eval_protocol: Prevalence analysis across 30 papers; controlled experiments showing each pitfall's inflation effect

title: SoK: Pragmatic Assessment of Machine Learning for Network Intrusion Detection
authors: Giovanni Apruzzese; Pavel Laskov; Johannes Schneider
venue: 2023 IEEE 8th European Symposium on Security and Privacy (EuroS&P)
dataset: Systematisation of NID papers plus large experimental campaign on public NID datasets (Sec. 5-6) and a practitioner survey
method: Defines 'pragmatic assessment': report what practitioners need (hardware, data pre-processing, costs, multiple datasets, statistical variance over many trials); hundreds of thousands of model runs to quantify variance
eval_protocol: Multiple random seeds/splits, multiple datasets, reporting of runtime and resources; shows how single-split results mislead

title: "Real Attackers Don't Compute Gradients": Bridging the Gap Between Adversarial ML Research and Practice
authors: Giovanni Apruzzese; Hyrum S. Anderson; Savino Dambra; David Freeman; Fabio Pierazzi; Kevin A. Roundy
venue: 2023 IEEE Conference on Secure and Trustworthy Machine Learning (SaTML)
dataset: Three industrial case studies (an online social network ML system; a commercial ML phishing-webpage detector; an ML evasion competition) plus analysis of recent adversarial-ML papers
method: Position paper contrasting research threat models with operational reality; case study (b) reports lack of evidence of gradient-based adversarial examples against a commercial phishing detector
eval_protocol: Qualitative; literature analysis

title: SpacePhish: The Evasion-space of Adversarial Attacks against Phishing Website Detectors using Machine Learning
authors: Giovanni Apruzzese; Mauro Conti; Ying Yuan
venue: Proceedings of the 38th Annual Computer Security Applications Conference (ACSAC 2022)
dataset: Two public phishing website datasets (Zenodo and delta-phish style collections; see Sec. 5 of PDF), 18 ML-PWD configurations
method: Formalises the 'evasion-space' (problem-space vs feature-space perturbations) and a realistic threat model; evaluates 12 cheap evasion attacks
eval_protocol: Statistical significance testing of detection-rate degradation across 18 detectors and 12 attacks, repeated trials

title: Towards benchmark datasets for machine learning based website phishing detection: An experimental study
authors: Abdelhakim Hannousse; Salima Yahiouche
dataset: New balanced dataset of 11,430 URLs with 87 features (56 URL, 24 content, 7 external services); phishing from PhishTank/OpenPhish, legitimate from Alexa-derived crawls with paths (Mendeley c2gw7fy2j4)
method: Reproducible dataset-construction scheme with guidelines (G1: collect from several sources; do not use Alexa domain lists directly because they lack sub-domains/paths); feature-importance and runtime analysis; comparison of classifiers
eval_protocol: Random stratified splits on the new dataset; feature relevance via several selectors

title: Reliability and Robustness analysis of Machine Learning based Phishing URL Detectors
authors: Bushra Sabir; M. Ali Babar; Raj Gaire; Alsharif Abuadbba
venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing
dataset: Reproduces 50 ML phishing-URL detectors; phishing URLs from PhishTank/OpenPhish/ISCXURL2016/PhishStorm (96,693); legitimate URLs crawled from 1,500 Alexa domains to obtain full paths; adversarial set 'Advdata' generated by URLBUG
method: Methodology to test reliability and robustness: adversarial URL generator (URLBUG), reproduction of 50 traditional-ML and DL detectors, evaluation on Advdata
eval_protocol: Baseline (balanced, in-distribution) vs adversarial URLs; MCC as main metric; registration-cost and real-world-use analysis of adversarial domains

title: Mitigating Bias in Machine Learning Models for Phishing Webpage Detection
authors: Aditya Kulkarni; Vivek Balachandran; Dinil Mon Divakaran; Tamal Das
dataset: Position paper; proposes generating synthetic phishing pages from legitimate URLs
method: Identifies dataset-assembly biases (imbalanced, non-diverse, stale datasets; zero-day gap) and proposes a tool to synthesise phishing pages for any set of legitimate URLs to debias/test detectors
eval_protocol: None reported (short paper)

title: ShieldPhish: Evaluating Representation Robustness and Cross-Source Generalization in Phishing URL Detection
authors: Gandhi Raj Giri
dataset: Lexical URL classifier trained on conventional public phishing/benign URL sets; post-freeze external snapshots: OpenPhish (phishing) and a Cisco Umbrella Top-1M snapshot (benign); domain-disjoint
method: Diagnoses 'representation shift' (models keying on https:// scheme and leading www.), introduces component-aware URL canonicalisation and hybrid rule fusion, then tests a frozen model on independently sourced, hash-verified post-freeze data
eval_protocol: Pre-registration-style freeze protocol; domain-disjoint external test; bootstrap 95% CIs; variant-stability tests (same URL re-formatted)

title: PhreshPhish: A Real-World, High-Quality, Large-Scale Phishing Website Dataset and Benchmark
authors: Thomas Dalton; Hemanth Gowda; Girish Rao; Sachin Pargi; Alireza Hadj Khodabakhshi; Joseph Rombs; Stephan Jou; Manish Marwah
dataset: New large phishing-website dataset (HTML+URL) crawled with a real browser, quality-checked by heuristics and human annotation; hosted on Hugging Face; benchmark subsets at base rates from 0.05% to 5%
method: Dataset construction pipeline: temporal train/test split, pruning of near-duplicate test points via locality-sensitive hashing, diversity/difficulty filters, base-rate adjustment; baseline models
eval_protocol: Temporal split + leakage pruning + five base rates; precision reported as a function of recall, FPR and base rate

title: SoK: PHILTER: Uncovering Security and Functional Gaps in AI-based Phishing Website Detection Literature via an LLM-based Reasoning Framework
authors: Mahbub Alam; Muhammad Lutfor Rahman; Sonjoy Kumar Paul; Amy W. Hays; Aftab Hussain; Md Imanul Huq; Nitesh Saxena
dataset: 55 academic AI-based phishing-website detection approaches assessed
method: LLM-assisted extraction plus expert validation against four functionality metrics (incl. F3 robustness on diverse benign pages, F4 evaluation transparency under class imbalance) and three security metrics (S1 adaptation to concept drift via temporally disjoint evaluation, S2 resistance to active attackers, S3 privacy)
eval_protocol: Rubric scoring of each paper; taxonomy of detection strategies

title: The Fragility of Phishing Detection Models: Evidence from Cross-Corpus Transfer, Prevalence Shift, Artifact Learning, and Evasion Risk
authors: Istiaque Bhuiyan; Tanvir Bhuiyan
dataset: Six public phishing/spam email corpora: CEAS_08, Enron, Ling, Nazario, Nigerian Fraud, SpamAssassin
method: TF-IDF logistic regression and linear SVC; pooled baseline, single-corpus cross-dataset transfer, leave-one-corpus-out, prevalence-shift simulation, training-prevalence manipulation, dataset-identification probe, top-feature inspection, artifact-removal ablation, feature-sensitivity masking
eval_protocol: Cross-corpus and leave-one-out; prevalence shift with fixed thresholds vs alert budgets; artefact ablations

title: Phishing URL detection generalisation using Unsupervised Domain Adaptation
authors: Fariza Rashid; Ben Doyle; Soyeon Caren Han; Suranga Seneviratne
dataset: Three phishing-URL datasets (abstract); pairwise cross-dataset experiments
method: Unsupervised domain adaptation framework to transfer URL classifiers between datasets
eval_protocol: Train on one dataset, test on another (cross-dataset F1), with and without adaptation

title: Can Features for Phishing URL Detection Be Trusted Across Diverse Datasets? A Case Study with Explainable AI
authors: Maraz Mia; Darius Derakhshan; Mir Mehedi A. Pritom
venue: Proceedings of the 11th International Conference on Networking, Systems, and Security (NSysS 2024)
dataset: Dataset-1: Vrbancic et al. (88,647 instances, 58,000 benign); Dataset-2: Kaggle set with 19,431 rows (9,716 benign); 20 overlapping numeric URL features
method: Train/test within and across datasets (Exp-1..6); SHAP global/local explanations to compare feature contribution
eval_protocol: Random splits within dataset; cross-dataset transfer on common features; merged training

title: Ensemble transfer learning for cross-dataset phishing detection
authors: Saviour Henry; Bliss Utibe-Abasi Stephen; Philip Asuquo
dataset: UCI Phishing Websites dataset and PhiUSIIL phishing URL dataset (zero feature overlap)
method: Cross-Domain Ensemble Probability Fusion: PCA harmonisation into a 20-dim space plus information-theoretic weighted fusion
eval_protocol: Cross-dataset accuracy before/after the framework

title: An effective detection approach for phishing websites using URL and HTML features
authors: Ali Aljofey; Qingshan Jiang; Abdur Rasool; Hui Chen; Wenyin Liu; Qiang Qu; Yang Wang
dataset: Self-built dataset of 60,252 webpages (32,972 benign, 27,280 phishing) plus a benchmark dataset for external validation
method: XGBoost on URL character sequences, hyperlink features and TF-IDF of noisy HTML/plaintext
eval_protocol: Evaluation on own dataset and on a second benchmark dataset (cross-dataset check)

title: PhiUSIIL: A diverse security profile empowered phishing URL detection framework based on similarity index and incremental learning
authors: Arvind Prasad; Shalini Chandra
dataset: PhiUSIIL Phishing URL dataset: 235,795 URLs (134,850 legitimate, 100,945 phishing) with 54 URL and page-derived features (UCI id 967)
method: Similarity-index features (URLSimilarityIndex etc.) plus incremental learning framework
eval_protocol: Not accessible (paywalled); UCI page gives dataset composition only

title: The base-rate fallacy and the difficulty of intrusion detection
authors: Stefan Axelsson
venue: ACM Transactions on Information and System Security
dataset: Analytical; no dataset
method: Bayesian analysis of detector alarms under low attack prevalence
eval_protocol: Shows that with realistic base rates the false-alarm rate dominates the Bayesian detection rate (positive predictive value)

title: Outside the Closed World: On Using Machine Learning for Network Intrusion Detection
authors: Robin Sommer; Vern Paxson
venue: 2010 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy
dataset: Position paper; no dataset
method: Analysis of why ML anomaly detection is rarely deployed: high cost of errors, semantic gap, diversity of traffic, difficulty of sound evaluation, adversarial setting
eval_protocol: Recommends evaluation with realistic data, understanding of what the system learns, and attention to false-positive cost

title: An In-Depth Benchmarking and Evaluation of Phishing Detection Research for Security Needs
authors: Ayman El Aassal; Shahryar Baki; Avisha Das; Rakesh M. Verma
dataset: New URL, website and email datasets with varying legitimate:phishing ratios; legitimate URLs from diverse sources rather than Alexa domain lists
method: PhishBench benchmarking framework; systematic feature taxonomies for URLs, websites, emails; evaluation of published methods under varying imbalance and dataset size; feature-importance and extraction-time analysis
eval_protocol: Balanced vs imbalanced ratios, scaling experiments, retraining on new attacks

title: Diverse Datasets and a Customizable Benchmarking Framework for Phishing
authors: Victor Zeng; Shahryar Baki; Ayman El Aassal; Rakesh M. Verma; Luis Felipe Teixeira De Moraes; Avisha Das
venue: Proceedings of the Sixth International Workshop on Security and Privacy Analytics (IWSPA '20)
dataset: Diverse phishing email, website and URL datasets released with PhishBench
method: Benchmarking framework (PhishBench) for features and classifiers
eval_protocol: Framework supports metrics beyond accuracy and imbalanced evaluation

title: Tranco: A Research-Oriented Top Sites Ranking Hardened Against Manipulation
authors: Victor Le Pochat; Tom Van Goethem; Samaneh Tajalizadehkhoob; Maciej Korczyński; Wouter Joosen
venue: Network and Distributed System Security Symposium (NDSS 2019)
dataset: Alexa, Cisco Umbrella, Majestic and Quantcast top lists over time; 133 security papers surveyed for top-list usage
method: Measurement of top-list instability and manipulability (demonstrates cheap insertion into Alexa); proposes Tranco aggregate list
eval_protocol: Longitudinal list comparison; manipulation experiments

title: A Long Way to the Top: Significance, Structure, and Stability of Internet Top Lists
authors: Quirin Scheitle; Oliver Hohlfeld; Julien Gamba; Jonas Jelten; Torsten Zimmermann; Stephen D. Strowes; Narseo Vallina-Rodriguez
venue: Proceedings of the Internet Measurement Conference 2018 (IMC '18)
dataset: Alexa, Umbrella, Majestic lists; survey of list use in measurement/security papers
method: Structural and stability analysis of top lists and their effect on research results
eval_protocol: Repeats several published measurements with different lists/dates to show result sensitivity

title: Decoding the Secrets of Machine Learning in Malware Classification: A Deep Dive into Datasets, Feature Extraction, and Model Performance
authors: Savino Dambra; Yufei Han; Simone Aonzo; Platon Kotzias; Antonino Vitale; Juan Caballero; Davide Balzarotti; Leyla Bilge
venue: Proceedings of the 2023 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS '23)
dataset: 67k Windows PE samples from 670 families (100 each) plus benign set; static and dynamic features
method: Controlled study of how dataset composition (families, samples per family, benign/malware balance), feature type and classifier drive reported performance
eval_protocol: Varies dataset properties systematically; family-aware splits

title: Challenges and pitfalls in malware research
authors: Marcus Botacin; Fabricio Ceschin; Ruimin Sun; Daniela Oliveira; André Grégio
dataset: Systematic review of 491 malware papers (2000-2018)
method: Literature review identifying 20 pitfalls (threat model, closed datasets, ground truth from closed-source AV, etc.)
eval_protocol: N/A

title: SoK: A Comprehensive Reexamination of Phishing Research From the Security Perspective
authors: Avisha Das; Shahryar Baki; Ayman El Aassal; Rakesh Verma; Arthur Dunbar
dataset: Systematisation of phishing detection literature (email, website, URL) against four 'security challenges': real-time detection, active attacker, dataset quality, base-rate fallacy
method: Critical survey with dataset-property, feature, algorithm and metric analysis
eval_protocol: Reviews evaluation practice and finds: use of balanced datasets and inappropriate metrics, unreported timings, lack of generalisation studies

title: Deep Learning for Phishing Detection: Taxonomy, Current Challenges and Future Directions
authors: Nguyet Quang Do; Ali Selamat; Ondrej Krejcar; Enrique Herrera-Viedma; Hamido Fujita
dataset: Systematic review of DL phishing-detection papers
method: Taxonomy of DL approaches; analysis of datasets, features, metrics, challenges
eval_protocol: Reports that many works train on old, non-diverse or highly imbalanced data and use accuracy on imbalanced sets

title: A Survey of Machine Learning-Based Solutions for Phishing Website Detection
authors: Lizhen Tang; Qusay H. Mahmoud
dataset: Survey; tabulates datasets (UCI, Mendeley, ISCXURL-2016, PhishTank/OpenPhish + Alexa/Common Crawl crawls)
method: Comparative review of ML solutions, features, datasets and reported accuracies
eval_protocol: Notes that many solutions report >99% accuracy on single datasets; Table 5 lists 'did not use multiple different datasets to train the model, compare the results' as a limitation

title: Phishing or Not Phishing? A Survey on the Detection of Phishing Websites
authors: Rasha Zieni; Luisa Massari; Maria Carla Calzarossa
dataset: Survey of list-based, similarity-based and ML-based detection; dataset sources (PhishTank, OpenPhish, Alexa, DMOZ, Google queries)
method: Structured review of features, selection, algorithms, metrics
eval_protocol: Notes that Alexa retired in May 2022 and DMOZ was discontinued, that datasets 'often share the data sources' yet differ in content, and highlights work demonstrating 'the importance of taking precisely into account the imbalanced nature of phishing attacks'

title: Malicious URL Detection using Machine Learning: A Survey
authors: Doyen Sahoo; Chenghao Liu; Steven C. H. Hoi
dataset: Survey; discusses URL data sources and 'detection as a service' design
method: Formalises malicious URL detection as ML; taxonomy of feature representations (blacklist, lexical, host, content, context) and learning algorithms incl. online learning
eval_protocol: Discusses practical issues: concept drift, label acquisition, feature cost; open problems
